info.title: Replicas API
info.description: Create and control workspaces, and manage the environments, automations, and learnings they run with.

get.description: Exports retained conversations from every replica without waking them. Requires an organization API key. Deleted chats and conversations outside your [data retention](/admin/data-retention) window are omitted.

parameters.name: cursor
parameters.description: Opaque cursor from `next_cursor`. It preserves the initial replica and environment filters and stable artifact creation order. Filters may be omitted on later requests but cannot be changed. Chat and replica deletion and restoration remain live and require restarting the export for a consistent total.

parameters.name: environment_id
parameters.description: Return conversations from replicas created with one environment.

post.description: Creates a replica from an environment and sends the first message. Returns immediately with `status: "preparing"`; use `GET /v1/replica/{id}/wait` to wait for it. An organization can have 100 API and automation replicas active or preparing at once.

404.description: Repository or repository set not found

429.description: The organization already has 100 metered API and Automation workspaces active or preparing

parameters.name: user_id

parameters.description: The unique identifier of the replica

parameters.name: include

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The unique identifier of the replica

post.description: Sends a message to a chat. Sleeping replicas wake and archived replicas restore first. Messages sent while the agent is working are queued.

parameters.name: id

get.description: Reads history from the newest event. Omit `limit` for everything. To page back, pass the previous `before_cursor` until it is `null`. Sleeping and archived replicas return retained history without waking. Returns `409` when a suspended replica has no retained history.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The unique identifier of the replica

parameters.name: chat_id
parameters.description: Filter history to a specific chat

parameters.name: limit
parameters.description: Maximum number of events to return, taken from the end of the history. Omit to return the full history.

parameters.name: before_event
parameters.description: Exclusive upper bound: return only events with an index below this value. Pass the previous response's `eventsStartIndex` to fetch the page before it. Indexes are stable as new events append to the end.

parameters.name: before_turn
parameters.description: Exclusive upper bound for Codex transcript turns, paged with `turnsStartIndex` the same way `beforeEvent` pages events.

parameters.name: before_cursor
parameters.description: Opaque cursor from the previous response's `beforeCursor`. Advances events and Codex turns together.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The unique identifier of the replica

get.description: Streams replica events as server-sent events (`data: <JSON>`). Each event has `id`, `ts`, `type`, and `payload`; see `EngineEvent` for types. A ping is sent every 15 seconds. The replica must be active, so send a message or wake it first.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The unique identifier of the replica

200.description: SSE event stream opened successfully. Each line is a JSON-encoded `EngineEvent`.

post.description: Starts waking a sleeping replica and returns `202` immediately. Set `restore=true` to also restore an archived replica. Replicas in `error` are retried. Sending a message wakes or restores a replica too.

parameters.name: restore
parameters.description: Restore the replica if it is archived

post.description: Pauses compute. The replica keeps its files and wakes on the next message.
Archives a replica. Sending a message or waking with `restore=true` restores it.

get.description: Lists media the replica uploaded, newest first. Fetch a file with [Get a media download URL](/api-reference/media/get-a-media-download-url).

Waits until the replica finishes starting and its agents finish their turns, then returns its chats. Returns `done: false` after `timeout_seconds` (max 50) if work is still running; call it again to keep waiting. Use [Stream events](/api-reference/replica/stream-events) for live updates.

parameters.name: id
parameters.description: The unique identifier of the replica

waking.description: If true, the workspace was sleeping and is now waking up. Retry after 30-90 seconds.

patch.description: Sets the objective of a Codex chat, or pauses and resumes it. Other agents return `goal: null`; give them a goal by sending a message with `goal_mode: true`. The replica must be active.

post.description: Answers a question or approval the agent is waiting on. Find pending requests in [Read history](/api-reference/replica/read-history): a tool call with `inputRequest.status` of `pending` carries the `request_id` and its option IDs.

200.description: Whether the request was still pending

post.description: Starts a new chat that continues from this chat's history, optionally on another coding agent and with a first message. The replica must be active.

get.description: Lists messages waiting for the agent to finish its turn.

post.description: Adds the queued message to the agent's current turn without stopping it.
Sends the queued message right away instead of waiting for the turn to finish. Running commands keep going in the background.

Runs a shell command and returns its output and exit code. Commands that outlast `timeout_seconds` are stopped and return `timed_out: true`. Use a terminal session for interactive or long-running work. The replica must be active.
Opens an interactive shell. Read output from Stream terminal output and write with Send terminal input. A replica can have 8 sessions. The replica must be active.
Writes keystrokes. Number writes with an increasing `sequence` and keep `generation` fixed for the session.

get.description: Server-sent events whose `data` is a JSON string of terminal output. The first event replays recent output.

post.description: Returns a short-lived token and proxy command for SSH. The [CLI](/features/cli) runs this for you. The replica must be active.
Returns state, checks, reviews, and mergeability for up to 20 pull requests the replica opened. Get URLs from Get replica.
Merges a GitHub pull request when it is open and mergeable. Returns `403` when the organization's security policy blocks agent merges.
Closes, approves, converts to draft, or marks ready a GitHub pull request the replica opened. Approving uses your GitHub account, so it needs a personal API key with GitHub connected.
Creates a public URL for a port. Set `authenticated` to require Replicas sign-in. Port 3737 is reserved for the Replicas engine. The replica must be active.

debounce_seconds.description: Seconds to wait for trigger events to stop before running once with the latest payload. GitHub and GitLab events debounce per pull or merge request. `null` or `0` disables debouncing.

github_check_names.description: Set or clear the GitHub check names this automation reports its verdict on. A non-empty list requires a pull_request.opened or pull_request.synchronize trigger. Pass an empty array to stop creating checks.

environment_id.description: Move this automation to a different environment.

workspace_auto_stop_minutes.description: New inactivity timeout in minutes for the default keep-alive policy (set to null to clear)

workspace_size.description: New compute size for every workspace this automation fires off. `small` (2 vCPU, 8 GB memory) bills at $0.008/min, `large` (4 vCPU, 16 GB memory) at $0.016/min, and `ultra` (8 vCPU, 32 GB memory) at $0.032/min.

agent_provider.description: New coding agent override. Null inherits the organization default.

model.description: New model override. Requires `agent_provider` when set. Must be a model your organization allows for that agent; hidden models are rejected with 400.

thinking_level.description: New thinking/reasoning level override. `ultra` is available for Codex and Muse Code; `ultracode` is Claude Code-only.

plan_mode.description: Enable or disable plan mode for automation messages.

goal_mode.description: Enable or disable goal mode for automation messages. Null inherits the resolved agent default; false explicitly disables it.

fast_mode.description: Enable or disable fast mode for automation messages. Null inherits the resolved agent default; false explicitly disables it.

TriggerAutomationRequest.description: Request body for manually triggering an automation

payload.description: Optional payload to pass to the automation execution

pr.description: Pull request to run against. Requires a GitHub `pull_request.command` trigger for that repository.

repository_id.description: The Replicas repository UUID the pull request belongs to

workspace_id.description: The workspace created for this execution

ListOrganizationAutomationExecutionsResp.description: Paginated list of executions across accessible automations

ClaudeEventPayload.description: Payload of a Claude Code agent event, wrapping the Claude SDK message.

subtype.description: Present on `claude-result` events; `success` indicates a clean turn completion. Any other value (e.g. `error`) signals a failed turn even when `is_error` is false.

parent_tool_use_id.description: If this message is the result of a sub-agent tool call, the parent tool_use ID

is_error.description: Present on `claude-result` events; true if the turn ended with an error

errors.description: Array of error messages, present on `claude-result` events when `is_error` is true

ClaudeMessage.description: A Claude SDK message containing an array of content blocks.

content.description: Ordered list of content blocks produced or consumed by the model.

ClaudeContentBlock.description: A single content block within a Claude message. Discriminated by `type`.

oneOf.title: TextBlock
oneOf.description: A text response from the model.

oneOf.title: ThinkingBlock
oneOf.description: An extended-thinking block showing the model's reasoning.

oneOf.title: ToolUseBlock
oneOf.description: A tool invocation by the model (e.g. Bash, Edit, Write, Grep, Glob, Read, WebSearch, TaskCreate, Skill).

id.description: Unique ID for this tool use, referenced by subsequent tool_result blocks

oneOf.title: ToolResultBlock
oneOf.description: The result of a tool invocation, sent back to the model in `claude-user` events.

tool_use_id.description: ID of the tool_use block this result corresponds to

content.description: Tool output — either a plain string or an array of text/image blocks.

is_error.description: Whether the tool execution resulted in an error

CodexAgentEvent.description: A streaming event from the Codex CLI agent. Uses either `event_msg` for high-level messages or `response_item` for structured response items.

type.description: `event_msg` carries high-level messages (user input, reasoning). `response_item` carries structured responses (assistant messages, function calls, tool calls).

CursorAgentEvent.description: A streaming event from the Cursor agent. Cursor events are normalized with a `cursor-` prefixed type and a provider payload.

type.description: Cursor event type. `cursor-assistant` contains model output, `cursor-thinking` contains reasoning text, `cursor-tool_call` contains tool progress/results, `cursor-task` contains task updates, `cursor-status` contains run status, and `cursor-error` contains failure details.

payload.description: Cursor event payload. Shape depends on the parent event `type`; Cursor payload sub-shapes are not yet formally specified.

MuseAgentEvent.description: A streaming event from Muse Code over Muse Server Protocol.

type.description: Muse event type. Item events carry assistant, reasoning, and tool updates; session events report usage; turn completion and error events describe terminal state.

payload.description: Muse event payload. Shape depends on the parent event type.

OpencodeAgentEvent.description: A streaming event from the Opencode agent. Opencode events are normalized with an `opencode-` prefixed type and an open provider payload.

type.description: Opencode event type. Common values include `opencode-message.updated`, `opencode-session.idle`, `opencode-error`, and `opencode-part-*` events.

payload.description: Opencode event payload. Shape depends on the parent event `type`; Opencode payload sub-shapes are not yet formally specified.

PiAgentEvent.description: A streaming event from the Pi coding agent. Pi events expose session lifecycle, text and reasoning updates, tool execution, and errors.

type.description: Pi event type. Common values include pi-message_update, pi-tool_execution_start, pi-tool_execution_update, pi-tool_execution_end, and pi-error.

payload.description: Pi event payload. Shape depends on the parent event type.

CodexEventPayload.description: Payload of a Codex CLI agent event. Shape depends on the parent event `type`.

CodexEventMsgPayload.description: Payload for `event_msg` events — high-level user or reasoning messages.

type.description: `user_message` for user input, `agent_reasoning` for the agent's chain-of-thought

message.description: User message text (present when type is `user_message`)

CodexResponseItemPayload.description: Payload for `response_item` events — structured items from the Codex response stream.

oneOf.title: AssistantMessage
oneOf.description: A text message from the Codex agent.

oneOf.title: FunctionCall
oneOf.description: A function call by the Codex agent (shell commands, plan updates).

call_id.description: Unique ID for this call, referenced by the corresponding `function_call_output`

arguments.description: JSON-encoded arguments (e.g. `{"command": "ls -la"}` for shell commands, `{"plan": [...]}` for plan updates)

oneOf.title: FunctionCallOutput
oneOf.description: Output from a previously invoked function call.

call_id.description: ID of the function_call this output corresponds to

output.description: Raw output string. For shell commands this may include exit codes and stdout/stderr.

oneOf.title: CustomToolCall
oneOf.description: A custom tool invocation (e.g. `apply_patch` for file edits).

oneOf.title: CustomToolCallOutput
oneOf.description: Output from a custom tool call.

call_id.description: ID of the custom_tool_call this output corresponds to

AccessGrant.description: A single grant. A null `resource_id` grants every resource of that type in the organization; a UUID grants only that resource. Write implies Read.

resource_id.description: Null means every resource of this type. Always null for `analytics`.

everyone.description: Grants that apply to every member of the organization.

scopes.description: Organization-wide scopes in effect for the caller, from grants whose `resource_id` is null. Admins hold every scope. Per-resource grants are not listed here; they appear as `access` on each record.

EnvironmentAccess.description: Effective permissions for the caller. Read allows discovery, full inspection, and selection for workspaces or automations. Write allows all mutations and implies Read.

Environment.description: The configuration a workspace starts with. The Global environment (`is_global: true`) applies to every workspace. Personal environments have `user_id` set and are visible only to their owner.

user_id.description: Owning user for personal environments. Null for team environments.

is_global.description: True for the org's singleton Global environment, whose values apply to every workspace. Global envs cannot be deleted, cannot be edited via PATCH, and have no repository binding.

repository_id.description: Bound repository ID. Mutually exclusive with `repository_set_id`. Both null = unbound repo-less workspace.

repository_set_id.description: Bound repository set ID. Mutually exclusive with `repository_id`.

system_prompt.description: Optional system prompt prepended to every workspace's coding agent.

mobile_testing_enabled.description: Whether workspaces from this environment receive mobile simulator access. Available on trial, Team, and Enterprise plans and configurable only on team environments.

personal_preferences.description: User-authored instructions appended after the (inherited) system prompt. Only settable on personal environments, and editable even when source-backed.

source_environment_id.description: Source team environment for source-backed personal environments. Null for standalone personal environments and team environments.

variable_count.description: Number of variables attached to this environment

access.description: Effective permissions for the authenticated member. Omitted from internal workspace-authenticated responses.

CreateEnvironmentRequest.description: Request body for creating a new environment.

name.description: Human-readable name (must be unique within the selected scope)

scope.description: `org` creates a team environment. `user` creates a personal environment visible only to the authenticated user.

source_environment_id.description: Optional shared source. Shared environments create an independent copy with the source access policy. Personal environments create a private overlay and keep inherited config locked.

repository_id.description: Bind to this repository. Mutually exclusive with `repository_set_id`.

repository_set_id.description: Bind to this repository set. Mutually exclusive with `repository_id`.

system_prompt.description: Optional system prompt prepended to the coding agent.

mobile_testing_enabled.description: Enable mobile testing. Only valid for team environments on trial, Team, and Enterprise plans; otherwise returns `PLAN_UPGRADE_REQUIRED`.

UpdateEnvironmentRequest.description: Request body for updating an environment. Only provided fields are changed. `repository_id` and `repository_set_id` remain mutually exclusive when both are supplied.

mobile_testing_enabled.description: Enable or disable mobile testing. Only valid on team environments; enabling requires a trial, Team, or Enterprise plan and otherwise returns `PLAN_UPGRADE_REQUIRED`.

personal_preferences.description: Only settable on personal environments. Appended after the (inherited) system prompt.

WorkloadIdentityResponse.description: Issuer configuration workspaces mint tokens against. Contains no token values.

McpWorkloadAuth.description: Authenticate using a short-lived workspace identity token minted for the given audience, or an OAuth account connected in the app.

audience.description: Audience (`aud`) the MCP server verifies, usually its URL.

EnvironmentVariable.description: An environment variable. Values are encrypted at rest and decrypted on read.

personal_override_allowed.description: Whether source-backed personal environments may override this inherited key

CreateEnvironmentVariableRequest.description: Request body for creating an environment variable.

personal_override_allowed.description: Team/Global variables only. Allows source-backed personal environments to override this inherited key.

UpdateEnvironmentVariableRequest.description: Request body for updating an environment variable. Only provided fields are changed.

personal_override_allowed.description: Team/Global variables only. Allows source-backed personal environments to override this inherited key.

EnvironmentFile.description: A file dropped into the workspace at the configured `path` when the workspace is provisioned.

path.description: Destination path inside the workspace (typically under `~/`)

CreateEnvironmentFileRequest.description: Request body for creating an environment file. Maximum content size is 64 KB (65,536 bytes).

path.description: Destination path inside the workspace, e.g. `~/AGENTS.md`

UpdateEnvironmentFileRequest.description: Request body for updating an environment file. Only provided fields are changed.

EnvironmentSkill.description: A skill enabled on an environment. The membership row, not the catalog entry.

source.description: Catalog URL or other source identifier

CreateEnvironmentSkillRequest.description: Request body for enabling a skill on an environment.

name.description: Display name (typically copied from the catalog result)

source.description: Catalog URL or other source identifier

RepoSkillFramework.description: Which AI tool owns the discovered file's on-disk convention.

RepoSkill.description: A skill/agent/command/prompt file discovered inside the environment's bound repo. Distinct from `EnvironmentSkill`: these are inferred live from the repo's git tree, are read-only, and have no DB row.

id.description: Stable id, formed from the repository UUID and the in-repo path.

branch.description: Default branch the file was resolved against.

path.description: Repo-relative path of the discovered file or skill directory.

name.description: Human-friendly name (from YAML frontmatter when present, otherwise the filename or directory).

description.description: Single-line description, populated from frontmatter when available.

error.description: Populated when discovery couldn't run end-to-end (e.g. the bound repo has no GitHub App installation). The list may still be partially filled; the UI shows this as an inline banner rather than a 5xx.

EnvironmentSkillsRegistry.description: A GitHub repository registered as a skill registry on an environment.

EnvironmentSkillsRegistryWithContents.description: A skill registry with its discovered skills.

installs.description: Approximate install count from the catalog

EnvironmentMcpStdioConfig.description: Configuration for an MCP that runs a local subprocess (`transport: stdio`).

EnvironmentMcpHttpConfig.description: Configuration for an MCP reached over HTTP or SSE (`transport: http` or `transport: sse`).

EnvironmentMcpConfig.description: MCP transport-specific configuration. Discriminate by the parent `transport` field.

EnvironmentMcp.description: An MCP (Model Context Protocol) server attached to an environment.

name.description: MCP name (1–64 chars, must match `^[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9_-]{0,63}$`; cannot start with reserved prefixes `relay-`, `replicas-`, or `subagents`)

oauth.description: Connection state for MCPs using OAuth. Returned when listing MCPs.

CreateEnvironmentMcpRequest.description: Request body for creating an MCP. The `config` shape must match the chosen `transport`.

name.description: 1–64 chars, `^[A-Za-z0-9][A-Za-z0-9_-]{0,63}$`; reserved prefixes `relay-`, `replicas-`, and `subagents` are rejected.

UpdateEnvironmentMcpRequest.description: Request body for updating an MCP. Only provided fields are changed. When `transport` is changed, `config` is required and must match the new transport's shape.

WarmHookRecord.description: A warm hook — the shell script that runs while pre-warming workspaces for an environment.

version.description: Monotonic version (newer scripts have higher versions)

is_active.description: Whether this version is the active one for the environment

WarmPoolConfigWithStats.description: Warm pool configuration plus current pool counts.

generation.description: Monotonic counter bumped on every invalidation. Workspaces and snapshots carry the generation they were built for; anything older is stale by derivation.

error_count.description: Consecutive reconcile failures since the last success. Resets to 0 on success; drives exponential backoff via `next_retry_at`.

next_retry_at.description: Earliest time the next reconcile pass may run for this config. Null when not in backoff.

last_error_at.description: When the most recent reconcile error was recorded (null if no current error).

last_error_message.description: Most recent reconcile error message (null if no current error).

has_base_snapshot.description: Whether the current generation has a base snapshot.

ready_count.description: Number of pre-warmed workspaces at the current generation that are ready to be assigned

stale_count.description: Number of ready workspaces at older generations. Still claimable as a fallback; trimmed by reconcile when over target.

warming_count.description: Number of workspaces at the current generation that are currently warming (warm hooks running)

snapshotting_count.description: Number of seed workspaces currently capturing a base snapshot (E2B only). Always 0 on providers without live snapshots.

last_failure_at.description: When the most recent warm-up failure occurred (null if never)

last_failure_reason.description: Reason for the most recent warm-up failure

WarmPoolSnapshotRecord.description: A retained provider snapshot for one successful warm-pool generation.

id.description: Snapshot record UUID used by the restore endpoint

generation.description: Warm-pool generation that captured this snapshot

is_current.description: Whether the config is currently installed on this snapshot. Restoring an older version moves this flag back onto that version.

is_fallback.description: Whether this snapshot is serving while the current generation warms or recovers

warm_hook.description: The active warm hook for the environment (null if none has ever been saved).

warm_pool.description: The warm pool config and current counts (null if no pool has been configured).

snapshots.description: Up to 20 retained snapshots ordered newest first.

WarmHookTestResult.description: Result of running a warm hook script in an isolated sandbox.

timed_out.description: Whether execution was killed for taking too long

content.description: Shell script to persist and activate
Shell script to save and execute

StartHookRecord.description: A start hook — the shell script that runs at workspace boot (after the warm sandbox is claimed) for an environment.

version.description: Monotonic version (newer scripts have higher versions)

is_active.description: Whether this version is the active one for the environment

start_hook.description: The active start hook for the environment (null if none has ever been saved).

content.description: Shell script to persist and activate. Empty content clears the active start hook.

start_hook.description: The saved active start hook, or null when the request cleared the active start hook.

StartHookTestResult.description: Result of running a start hook script in an isolated sandbox.

timed_out.description: Whether execution was killed for taking too long

enabled.description: Whether the warm pool should be active

restored_generation.description: Generation of the snapshot that was restored and is now installed

WarmPoolWorkspaceRecord.description: A single pre-warmed workspace within a warm pool.

generation.description: Config generation this workspace was built for. Less than the parent config's `generation` means stale by derivation.

channel_id.description: Slack channel ID containing the thread.

workspace_id.description: Target workspace ID. Required outside agent mode.

name.description: Skill name from the SKILL.md frontmatter

description.description: When agents should use the skill

content.description: SKILL.md with `name` and `description` frontmatter. `description` should start with "Use when".

title.description: Short title, like "Always use Conventional Commits"

command.description: Shell command, run in the workspace root

output.description: Combined stdout and stderr, last 64 KB

system.description: Set on previews Replicas creates, like the live desktop stream on port 6080

CredentialStatus.description: Secrets are masked for API keys.
